messages:
liam wong: Hi all, new here. Trying to run the local stack on an M1 Mac. docker compose brings up redis fine but postgres crashes during init with "permission denied" on ./pgdata.

liam wong: Logs: 
```
postgres_1  | initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
postgres_1  | initdb: ensuring permissions of existing directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
```

rachael (eng): welcome! :wave: This is a known macOS bind-mount issue. Quick workaround: switch to a named docker volume instead of mounting a host folder. We keep host mounts limited to static fixtures only.

nick infra: also check the image arch. On M1 sometimes docker pulls amd64 and runs under qemu, which can change behavior. Add `platform: linux/arm64` to the postgres service in compose.yml if needed.

liam wong: swapped to `dev_pgdata` named volume, postgres starts but my app says connection refused. Postgres log shows it's only listening on a unix socket.

rachael (eng): make sure ports are mapped: `ports: - "5432:5432"` and `POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_PASSWORD/POSTGRES_DB` envs match your .env. In our dev compose we also set `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata` so paths line up.

devbot: Internal doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#postgres-local

liam wong: adding `platform: linux/arm64` fixed the arch issue, postgres is up and app connects. One last problem: our `scripts/db-reset` does host `dropdb` and fails because it tries to access files in the docker volume and permission denied. Any pattern to avoid that?

nick infra: best practice: run DB CLI inside the container, not touching volume files from host. Example: `docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1"`. For scripted tasks we use a helper script that runs a short psql container with proper envs.

rachael (eng): If you really want host postgres (fast iteration), install via Homebrew and point DATABASE_URL at it, but note CI and team tooling expect containerized DB. We'll add a note to onboarding about M1 + `platform` and named volumes.

liam wong: thanks all! resolved for me. I'll update my personal onboarding checklist. :tada:
